hints.title: 1 · Define replay before writing code
hints.body: Write a table for first request, identical retry, changed retry, and another customer with the same key. A retry must look up the old order before testing current inventory.

hints.title: 2 · Make the database change atomic
hints.body: A fictional reservation: Product.transaction do; decrement stock conditionally; Reservation.create!(...); end. A later exception must roll back the earlier write. Use a compound unique index for scope, rather than only a model uniqueness validation.

hints.title: 3 · Separate guarantees
hints.body: Use a conditional UPDATE with stock >= quantity and check the affected row count. Put the order and inventory change in the same transaction. Database check constraints defend writes that bypass validations. Explain duplicate-key races separately; this SQLite exercise does not certify multi-process correctness.

criteria.title: Replay semantics
criteria.target: Identical requests return the original order, changed payloads conflict, and keys are customer-scoped.
criteria.probe: Why must a replay work after inventory reaches zero?
criteria.practice: Write the retry state table from memory.

criteria.title: Atomic persistence
criteria.target: Stock and order commit together; unexpected failures propagate and roll back; rejected requests reserve no key.
criteria.probe: What happens if the database fails between decrement and order insert?
criteria.practice: Inject a write failure and inspect both persisted records.

criteria.title: Database defenses
criteria.target: Composite uniqueness, nonnegative stock, and positive quantity hold even for direct writes.
criteria.probe: Why is validates uniqueness insufficient under concurrent requests?
criteria.practice: Translate a correctness invariant into a unique index or check constraint.

criteria.title: Scope and concurrency judgment
criteria.target: State which guarantees tests demonstrate and what remains for concurrent PostgreSQL execution.
criteria.probe: How would you recover a lost response during simultaneous retries?
criteria.practice: Sketch a concurrent timeline and a database-specific recovery approach.

follow_up: Design concurrent checkout in PostgreSQL: same-key races, lock ordering, deadlock recovery, uniqueness errors, and retry boundaries. No external payment happens inside a retryable database transaction.
